subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw support caller-directed tool-result lifecycle control as destructive clearing, model-context-only masking, or recoverable archival, and which public adapters should expose it?
rationale: The implementation would create a new core context/session API surface that affects persistence, transcript replay, recovery, authorization, and compaction behavior; automation should not choose those product and safety semantics.

options.title: Design Canonical Archive/Clear Contract
options.body: Define stable IDs, auth, persistence, recovery, replay, and adapter semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep Automatic Pruning Only
options.body: Decline manual clearing for now and improve the existing TTL pruning, truncation, compact, reset, and docs paths.

options.title: Implement Narrow Destructive Clear
options.body: Add clear-by-id only, accepting that recovery and audit semantics are deliberately minimal.

recommendation.title: Design Canonical Archive/Clear Contract
recommendation.body: Define stable IDs, auth, persistence, recovery, replay, and adapter semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the cache-TTL pruning mode and adjacent product-review context for this exact issue family.
